title: John Williams and his combo join the Harris show
summary: John Williams, whom she later married, joined the Buzzin' Harris show in Cleveland with a combo, won her mother's confidence, and had a trombonist, Sylvester Briscoe, who played with his foot.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: After the home talent show what happened next?
John Williams - I later married him, you know, my first husband - joined up with the Harris Buzzin' Harris show in Cleveland.
You went out twice with that show?
I went out twice. The second time John Williams and his combo joined it.
But the first time was just summer vacation?
And then in about a year or so, was this a summer vacation?

I really don't know whether it was summer vacation but I decided to go out and stay out, which I didn't. I had to come back and go to school again. I went to Cleveland and several other places and by that time John Williams had joined with a small combo and he won my mother's confidence. He was very smart. He really should have been a psychiatrist because the things he did to help Andy Kirk in the band, keeping him down dissenting and all that and making a guy play and do his instrument was really terrific.
How old was he when you first met him?
He must have been around 19 or 20. I think he's about 5 or 6 years older than I am, something like that.

Yes, I was... He had a small combo, it was the most terrific thing you've ever heard in your life. See, John was the first musician that ever played a baritone and he was really in demand all over the country, everybody heard about him. But he chose to work with other people, you know, and he had his own little combo. We had a trombone player there that played more trombone with his foot than I hear today.
Sylvester Briscoe. His music was just terrific.
